To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spherical shape of a cell is unstable to perturbations of the cell wall curvature, and that the instability can lead to the formation of anisotropic shapes, which can include the formation of a cell wall protrusion, a cell wall depression or the formation of a ring-like structure.
we identify the parameters that determine pattern selection in a biomechani-cal model of cell wall growth, and that we identify a new mechanism for pattern selection in the growth of cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of pattern selection in a biome- chanical model for the three-dimensional growth of walled plant cells.
the analysis of the stability of a radially symmetric configuration of a cell wall in the linear regime and the study of the pattern selection in the non-linear regime.
the analysis of a model for cell growth and the identification of the possible mechanisms that can lead to the formation of non-radially symmetric shapes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a large range of the model parameters, the spherical configuration is linearly stable, but the nonlinear analysis reveals that it may be unstable and that, in this case, the final configuration is a nonradially symmetric shape.
a radially symmetric configuration is stable for small values of the nonlinearity, but unstable for large values of the non-linearity.
the model predicts the formation of patterns in the form of rings and/or spirals, depending on the values of the parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cell growth model is stable if the coupling is nonlinear or if the Poisson's ra-tio of the cell wall is large, but it is unstable otherwise.

, in both two- and three-dimensional cases, the cell wall expansion is stable for small values of the nonlinearity parameter and for large values of the effective diffusion of building material and Poisson's ratio.
the model predicts that, depending on the values of the parameters, the cell wall may grow in different shapes, including spherical, cylindrical and conical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell growth is a complex dynamical system that can exhibit rich pattern selection.
the anisotropy of the cell wall can lead to a variety of different patterns.
the anisotropic growth of a cell wall can be a mechanism to generate complex shapes, such as the one of a plant cell, in the absence of external cues.
